title: City-wide Expansion of Public Hygiene Infrastructure / Toilets, Hand Washing Stations and Permanent Water Spigots / Future Administrative Responsibility
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Administrative Officer, in coordination with the Bureau of Street Services, the Bureau of Sanitation, the Depattment of Water and Power, the Los Angeles County OCT 2 1 2026 Metropolitan Transportation Authority, and the Board of Public Works to report within 60 days with recommendations for a City-wide expansion of public hygiene infrastructure, including toilets, hand washing stations, and permanent water spigots. The report should include: • Opportunities for public-private partnerships, such as the Hollywood Partnership's funding and operation of 40 public bathroom stalls in Hollywood on the ground floor of the City's 1627 Vine Street garage; • Opportunities to provide public restroom and handwashing facilities on City and County-owned property, including potential locations within the public right-of-way and at or near Metro station entrances; determine whether Homeless Housing, Assistance and Prevention (HHAP) Program funds may be used for this purpose; and explore a funding partnership with the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health; • A status update on the implementation of DWP's Hydration Station Initiative Program and opportunities to partner with the City on installation of additional hydration stations. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Administrative Officer, with the assistance of the Chief Legislative Analyst, City Attorney, Bureau of Street Services, Board of Public Works, LA Sanitation and Environment, and Department of General Services, evaluate and recommend the appropriate department or office to assume responsibility for the administration, operation, maintenance, and future expansion of the public toilet program cmrently administered by the Bureau of Street Services. [ FURTHER MOVE that the City Administrative Officer, in coordination with the Bureau of Sanitation, Bureau of Street Services, and Board of Public Works, report within 60 days regarding the identification of continued, stable funding for the operational Skid Row public toilets, independent of and in addition to any funding identified for the City-wide expansion described above, so that existing service is preserved regardless of the timeline or outcome of that expansion. The report should also include identified funding for the ongoing provision of feminine hygiene products at all City-operated and City-funded public toilet and hygiene facilities, including whether Homeless Housing, Assistance and Prevention (HHAP) Program funds could support this provision.
